assumptions.statement: Room areas are measured to wall centerlines; net floor areas are smaller.

assumptions.basis: typical values for a first layout, not a regulation
assumptions.statement: Floor-to-floor height 3 m; split levels step in half storeys of 1.5 m; walls 2.8 m high.

assumptions.basis: typical thicknesses for a first layout
assumptions.statement: Exterior and retaining walls 0.3 m, partitions 0.15 m thick; no structural design has been done.
Plan grid: u axis along the parcel edge nearest road road-uphill.
Initial entry reference from the mean surveyed ground along the road-side face (11.70 m local), interpolated from the survey TIN (inferred).
Garage: separate road-level volume 6 × 6 m beside the entry bar (DEC-12).

Floor elevations and bar positions/lengths solved jointly with TIN lookup; sectional contact bands and circulation/daylight objectives, no excavation/void penalty. Earthworks evaluated exactly afterward.
Stair risers at most 0.18 m with 0.28 m goings; typical comfortable geometry, not checked against any code.

assumptions.basis: program cars (or a typical car) with the vehicle template's clearances and walls (S10-19)
assumptions.statement: The garage is a separate road-level volume, 6 m wide and 6 m deep for its cars (DEC-12).

assumptions.basis: solver closes every row of the massing
assumptions.statement: Rows are closed with flexible spaces that are not in the program (storage, or space to give back).
The plan is kept inside the buildable envelope (synthetic setbacks (3 m road side, 2 m sides, 3 m rear) invented for the example; not a zoning rule).
Level elevations, earth contact and retaining walls are inferred by linear interpolation of the surveyed points; ground between survey points is not verified.
